subject: Biotechnology
title: EU vs US Biotech Regulation
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: EU vs US Biotech Regulation.

hook.text: Same technology, opposite rules — the EU regulates the process of making GMOs while the US regulates the product itself.

buildup.text: The EU requires pre-market authorization, traceability, and labeling for all GMOs — precaution-based regulation.

discovery.text: The US splits oversight across FDA, EPA, and USDA — each evaluates whether the product is safe, regardless of how it was made.

twist.text: Gene-edited crops with no foreign DNA escape US regulation — but the EU Court ruled gene editing is GMO regulation territory.

climax.text: Argentina, Brazil, and Japan follow product-based approaches — the global patchwork creates trade barriers for biotech companies.

punchline.text: Same science, different rules — regulatory divergence shapes global biotech.

quiz.question: How does the EU regulate gene-edited crops differently from the US?
options: The EU does not regulate gene-edited crops at all
The EU treats gene-edited crops as GMOs requiring full authorization, while the US exempts those without foreign DNA
Both the EU and US regulate gene-edited crops identically
